replies.text:
Royal Malay Regiment (Askar Melayu): Expanded from 2 battalions after WWII to 7 battalions during the Emergency, comprised entirely of ethnic Malay soldiers who conducted regular jungle patrols against the insurgents.
Royal Malayan Police & Special Constabulary: To combat the insurgency, the British and local administration expanded the police force rapidly. By the early 1950s, over 20,000 Regular Police and 40,000+ Special Constables (who guarded estates, mines, and villages) were recruited—the overwhelming majority of whom were ethnic Malays.
Home Guard: Over 200,000 local volunteers were mobilized to protect villages and rural settlements, again with massive Malay participation across the Malay kampungs.

replies.author: @Henry4th
replies.text:
​@danielch6662WWII (1941–1945): Ethnic Chinese civilians suffered massive casualties not because they were all combatants, but because the Japanese Imperial Army systematically targeted them through brutal campaigns like Sook Ching due to the ongoing Second Sino-Japanese War.

Malayan Emergency (1948–1960): Out of ~2,400 civilians killed by the MNLA/MCP, the vast majority were non-Malay rubber estate workers, tin miners, and isolated villagers. They were executed or ambushed for refusing to pay "protection money," refusing to supply food, or for being suspected government informers. These were innocent victims, not casualties of people actively enlisting to fight for a country.
